findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method with that name is the one added in this PR in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm: protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the class hierarchy, so the services module fails to compile with 'no suitable method found: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()'. The call almost certainly should be isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), matching how the same method is invoked in UsernamePasswordForm.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, which disables passkeys on all fresh logins
findings.body: The new helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null, and it now gates every call to webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context): in authenticate() (line 115) and in challenge(context, error, field) (line 137). On an initial login there is no user in the authentication context (context.getUser() == null), so fillContextForm is never invoked for first-time logins: the WebAuthn challenge note, the ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI form attribute, and the webauth form markup are never set. Previously fillContextForm was called precisely in the user == null branch. This inverts the behavior and removes passkey autofill/auto-login from the normal (non re-authentication) username/password page, regressing the primary passkeys scenario. The tests retained/added in this very PR confirm the expected behavior and would fail: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey expects automatic passkey login when opening a fresh login form, and passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (in both PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) asserts that //form[@id='webauth'] is present on the fresh login page. The condition must also be true when the user is null (fresh login); requiring user != null makes passkeys available only during re-authentication.
